fieldworkDocument.title: Measgaichte / Miscellaneous
fieldworkDocument.note: [NOTES: some notes added (most probably by K. D. MacDonald?). See below for details.]

item.description: a circular stone wall built outdoors in which a fire would be lit. Not very high.
a chimney. Unusual to have this ‘w’ sound and you might be able to spell it better. Must be a variation on ‘luidhair’. [NOTES: note added above ‘w’ in ‘wuidhain’ – l?]
applied to a good going fire.
sarking.
a rope tied bits of wood together instead of using nails as we do nowadays.
an instrument used for making rope. Consisted of a bit of cylindrical wood with a hook at one end for twisting the heather, mane or whatever. [NOTES: a question mark added in the margin.]
work that involved carrying heavy weights on your shoulders.
applied to the bit of wood which stretched across a horse’s back and which were [sic] used to carry baskets.
damp.
a canvas bag able to take 140 lbs of weight.
this was a wooden tub which could hold the contents of one of these bags [i.e. poca bolla (q.v.)]. [NOTES: note added – from ‘bushel’.]
1 peck. A round barrel with a division in the middle which could be inserted so you could get a half peck. This was the instrument which the miller used to calculate his fee.
bottom of something.

this was the name given to the miller’s fee or payment. Everyone that used the mill had to pay a fee according to the amount of flour they left with. [NOTES: note added above ‘moughtainn’ – mobhdainn.]
exchange.
mill wheel.
mechanical wheels with iron teeth which gripped against each other helping to drive the mill wheel.
a screw which could be tightened or loosened depending on whether you wanted coarse or fine grain.
this was the chute which carried the water down to the mill wheel. [NOTES: corrected to ‘truinnse’.]
bits of wood on the actual mill wheel which caught the descending water and helped in the revolving process. Like wooden steps.
grinding stone.
a wooden chest with sides and four legs. The flour gathered here after being ground.
process whereby the grinding stones were serviced. The stones were roughened by a chipping hammer so that they would perform more effectively.
derricks. Used for hoisting the stones when they were to be serviced.
a drink made from barley. Nutritious. [NOTES: note added – cf. cabhraich.]
a home-made beer consisting of water, sugar, treacle and hops.
chaff.
dusk. Describes an evening when it was not fully dark. [NOTES: corrected to ‘rocach’.]
the hair on a horse’s lower foot. [NOTES: corrected to ‘mogain’.]
wooden wedges which were pointed.
wooden hammers for striking the above wedges [i.e. geindean (q.v.).]
weights and measures.
yellowy, slimy sand which was dangerous if a person entered such an area. No grounding. Very much like a quagmire.

item.headword: duine coingais air mùir neo tìr
item.description: describes a capable and fit man. A fit person is more accurate. [NOTES: ‘coingais’ underlined and a question mark added in the margin.]

this describes that feature of a window frame which has a lipped design. Especially in older windows, most of the wood on the inside of a window is finished in a curved or pointed style. Difficult to describe in words.
something that is common. [NOTES: corrected to ‘lianail’.]
another name for a small corn rick. More often called a ‘toit’.
for an accumulation or a batch of some commodity or other. More often this would be expressed as ‘tonn’ in Uist. “Fhuair mi deagh thonn mònadh dhachaidh an diugh.”
[See meall.]
usually seen in the late afternoon. A pattern of light lines is visible on the grass. Indicative of rain to follow.
two wooden tressels [sic] [trestles?] evenly spaced out. Beam of wood would then be cut. Perhaps this should be ‘slòc’ and not ‘sòc’. [NOTES: ‘sòc’ corrected to ‘soc’ and ‘sabhaidh’ to ‘sàbhaidh’.]
this was the term applied to all the dressing that was needed in preparing a coffin. Included nails, handles, linen, brass plates, etc. [NOTES: corrected to ‘muntadh’.]
a large river which is left on the shore once the tide has ebbed.
estate.
ramshackle.
a makeshift repair or more precisely someone who was noted for making such repairs. [NOTES: note added above ‘u’ in ‘splughan / splughadh’ – a.]
in these parts. “A bheil sion a’ dol a bhos ’s na costraichean seo?”
